registry.asserts: Every pad `requires` names a pad that exists.
registry.why: A typo here silently makes a pad unreachable for a whole run.

registry.asserts: Every structure pad's `buildAt` sits inside its tier, with its whole footprint.
registry.why: A building half outside the wall is a building raiders walk past.

registry.asserts: No two build mats overlap each other.
registry.why: Two mats on one spot means one of them can never be paid.

registry.asserts: The hand-placed opening homes are inside the tier-0 plot and clear of each other.
registry.why: They are coordinates typed by hand (#152), which is exactly what drifts.

registry.asserts: No `:root` token is defined as itself; any nothing reads is named.
registry.why: `--figure: var(--figure)` shipped -- a cycle, so six rules fell back to inherit and no number was gold.

registry.asserts: Every `icon:` named in config exists in the icon set.
registry.why: A missing icon draws nothing and says nothing.

registry.asserts: Every upgrade writes a mod that exists in MODS.
registry.why: An upgrade onto a misspelled key is a reward that does nothing, and nothing says so.

registry.asserts: Every structure kind a pad can build has a footprint.
registry.why: `placeOk` falls back to 3x3 for anything missing, which silently mis-sizes collisions.

registry.asserts: All twelve `?view=` URLs reach a running game with their panel open and filled.
registry.why: The board is iframes of these. A frame that opens on the wrong thing looks exactly like one that opened on the right thing.

registry.asserts: The King cannot cross a wall section: pushed at it from every side, he stays out.
registry.why: Asked for by name. A wall that can be walked through is not a wall.

registry.asserts: Every gate can be walked through, in both directions.
registry.why: The other half of the same question -- a wall with no way in is a cage.

registry.asserts: Sampling the whole wall ring, every point is either solid or a known gate.
registry.why: Asked for by name: "there is no gaps between gates".

registry.asserts: The snatch lands even if the King runs flat out from the moment it starts.
registry.why: It did not, for one commit: knights are slower than he is and the run stalled for ever.

registry.asserts: Through the whole calm, Wren is on the ground, outside the Keep, and not inside the King.
registry.why: Both bugs this scene has had were invisible to every other assertion.

registry.asserts: After the fall the plot is empty, the ledger is clear, and the first mat can be bought.
registry.why: The fall clears a lot of state by hand; anything it misses is unreachable progress.

registry.asserts: The calm is long enough to look around and short enough to replay.
registry.why: Thirty seconds is reasoned, not played. Only somebody playing it knows.

registry.asserts: The opening kingdom looks like a place somebody lives.
registry.why: Four homes in a row along the south is a first guess. `/board/` exists to judge it.

registry.asserts: A reward card can be read and ranked in the seconds a paused raid gives you.
registry.why: #107, #115 and #177 are all the same complaint arriving again.

registry.asserts: The game looks like one thing: one palette, one button, one voice.
registry.why: #135. A machine cannot tell you the game has drifted from its own guide.
